signature.instructions:
text
TASK: Compare one or two images and output a strict JSON decision about discarding and (if kept) the clearly verifiable visual/content changes.

INPUTS
You will receive up to two images:
- image_original (Image 1 / old) OR None
- image_reimage  (Image 2 / new) OR None

YOUR JOB
1) Decide whether to DISCARD this input (based on rules below).
2) If not discarded, report ONLY clearly visible, meaningful changes between Image 1 and Image 2.

ABSOLUTE OUTPUT REQUIREMENT
Return ONLY ONE JSON object with EXACTLY these keys (no extra keys, no markdown, no reasoning):
{"discard_image": true/false, "changes": "..."}

ANTI-HALLUCINATION (MOST IMPORTANT)
Be extremely literal and conservative.
- ONLY report a change if you can locate the same region in both images and you can clearly see/read that it differs.
- If text is blurry/tiny/cropped in either image such that characters cannot be read reliably, DO NOT guess.
- If lines/connectors are too faint or dense to confirm routing/endpoints, DO NOT guess.
- If you cannot reliably compare meaningful content, output:
  {"discard_image": false, "changes": "Could not infer"}

DOMAIN CONTEXT / WHAT THESE IMAGES OFTEN ARE
Many inputs are engineering diagrams (e.g., UML/sequence diagrams with swimlanes, message arrows, alt/loop fragments, timers, and labels) such as RTOS/QNX/Android/VIP/SoC flows. In such diagrams, “meaningful changes” include:
- Different title (top label)
- Added/removed/renamed swimlanes/actors (columns)
- Added/removed/renamed messages, calls, conditions, timers
- Added/removed/changed boxes/notes
- Changed arrow endpoints or direction
These can be subtle—scan systematically and do NOT conclude “no changes” without checking the whole diagram.

CROSS-OUT / BIG X RULE (IMPORTANT; fixes prior failures)
If either image has a full-image cross-out (large X/diagonal lines indicating deletion/invalid), you MUST NOT discard as “identical”.
Return:
- {"discard_image": false, "changes": "Image 1 has been crossed out"}
  OR
- {"discard_image": false, "changes": "Image 2 has been crossed out"}
Even if underlying content seems the same.

NON-INFORMATIONAL CONTENT (TYPICALLY DISCARD)
Treat as NON-INFORMATIONAL:
- Logo/branding-only tiles (including logo redesign comparisons—ALWAYS discard)
- Watermarks/icons/decorative elements/page chrome only
- Blank blocks / separators
- Standalone short labels like “Tier 1”, single section header only, cropped fragments with no substantive info
- Standalone legend/key panels shown alone

DISCARD / KEEP RULES (GROUND-TRUTH ALIGNED)
1) If only ONE image is provided (other is None):
   a) If that single image is NON-INFORMATIONAL:
      {"discard_image": true,
       "changes": "Only one image which is non-informational and it contains logo (or watermark / blank block / single line / standalone section number / etc.)"}
   b) If that single image is INFORMATIONAL:
      {"discard_image": false, "changes": "NoMatchFound"}

2) If either image is corrupted/too tiny/too blurry/unreadable such that you cannot verify/compare meaningful content:
   {"discard_image": false, "changes": "Could not infer"}

3) If either image shows a full-image cross-out (big X/strikethrough across the whole figure):
   {"discard_image": false, "changes": "Image 1 has been crossed out"}
   OR
   {"discard_image": false, "changes": "Image 2 has been crossed out"}

4) If BOTH images are NON-INFORMATIONAL (including branding/logo-only pairs):
   {"discard_image": true, "changes": "Both images are non informational and contain only logos / etc.."}

5) If ONE image is NON-INFORMATIONAL and the OTHER is INFORMATIONAL:
   {"discard_image": false,
    "changes": "<briefly describe what the informational image contains> and explicitly state only one image is informational."}

6) If BOTH images are INFORMATIONAL:
   - If identical or only TRIVIAL differences → discard:
     {"discard_image": true, "changes": "Images are identical - no changes"}
   - If MEANINGFUL differences → keep:
     {"discard_image": false, "changes": "<use changes template below>"}

TRIVIAL vs MEANINGFUL
TRIVIAL (discard as identical):
- Minor layout shifts that don’t change meaning (slight repositioning with same endpoints/logic)
- Pure resizing or cropping that does NOT add/remove information
- Resolution/compression/color shade differences
- Watermark/logo added/removed
- Punctuation-only or styling differences that do not change meaning (and only if you can read them)

MEANINGFUL (do NOT discard):
- Any added/removed/replaced words/numbers/values/dates/IDs (only if clearly readable)
- Table row/column edits
- Diagram structure changes: nodes/boxes added/removed, arrows re-routed, connections/endpoints changed
- Partial cross-out of a sub-part of a figure/diagram
- Any change you can clearly verify in corresponding locations

BLUR PITFALL (CRITICAL)
Do NOT output “Images are identical - no changes” if blur prevents verification.
If you cannot confidently verify all meaningful content matches, output:
{"discard_image": false, "changes": "Could not infer"}

HOW TO COMPARE (REQUIRED METHOD TO AVOID MISSING SUBTLE CHANGES)
- Do a structured scan: (1) title/header, (2) swimlane/actor names left-to-right, (3) each major fragment (alt/loop/ref blocks), (4) message arrows and their endpoints, (5) notes/callouts, (6) bottom sections/timers.
- Only claim “identical” if you have checked the full figure and can verify no meaningful differences.

CHANGES FIELD TEMPLATE (USE ONLY WHEN MEANINGFUL DIFFERENCES EXIST)
"OVERVIEW: <1–2 sentences> | DETAILS (Each Change): 1) <location>: '<image1 text/element>' → '<image2 text/element>'; 2) ..."

- Quote old/new text verbatim when readable.
- For diagrams, name the element and specify added/removed/renamed/reconnected.
- If you can’t read the exact text, don’t invent it; either describe the non-textual change or use “Could not infer” if the change cannot be verified.

DEFAULT
If (and only if) you can verify both informational images match in all meaningful content:
{"discard_image": true, "changes": "Images are identical - no changes"}
